entry.evidence: The uneven nature of a cut sediment surface results in topographic distortion in photos (Fig. 1).

steps.action: States the problems of core photography: glare, topographic distortion from uneven cut surfaces, and the many photos and long exposure to air that existing centre-stripe methods need.
steps.quote: The uneven nature of a cut sediment surface results in topographic distortion in photos (Fig. 1).

steps.action: Proposes computational photogrammetry (SFM-MVS) as an alternative that produces orthographic core photos from 10-20 overlapping photos per metre, whatever the surface topography.
steps.quote: This method requires only a small number (typically 10–20) of photographs for each metre of core

steps.action: Sets the aim of extending Jacq et al. (2021) by quantifying reconstruction and orthoimage quality across 22 SFM-MVS scenarios.
steps.quote: We expand upon their work by quantifying the quality of 3D reconstruction and orthoimagery for 22 different SFM-MVS scenarios.

steps.action: Builds the camera rig (a sliding 3D-printed hook on a pole between tripods), computes the geometry for 0.05 mm pixels, chooses an 80 mm equivalent focal length, sets exposure with test photos, and sets photo spacing for more than 60% overlap and diffuse lighting.
steps.quote: calculations were performed to determine the appropriate camera arrangement for a per-pixel resolution of 0.05 mm

steps.action: Defines the processing workflow: raw images with minimal adjustment in DXO, no sharpening, no lens-distortion pre-correction, and Agisoft Metashape on High settings for alignment, dense cloud, mesh and orthomosaic.
steps.quote: Agisoft Metashape Pro 1.7.4 (https://www.agisoft.com) was used for SFM-MVS processing of each sediment core segment.

steps.action: Sets laboratory conditions: a printed core orthoimage glued to a wooden beam (the beamcore), 40 mm above the table, with one corner twisted up by about 4 mm to simulate an uneven cut.
steps.quote: One corner of the beamcore was twisted upwards by ~ 4 mm to simulate lake cores

steps.action: Places 30 coded targets and six natural-feature check points, and measures their 3D coordinates twice each with a Leica total station and mini prism in a local coordinate system.
steps.quote: Targets were then located with a Leica 1203 TCRP total station and a GMP101 mini prism.

steps.action: Designs 22 scenarios (A-V) that vary target configuration, calibrated versus SFM-derived lens parameters, and measured versus assumed Z, with acceptance set as check-point error IQRs within 0.5 mm in XY and ±1 mm in Z.
steps.quote: An accuracy of 0.5 mm in the XY plane and ± 1 mm in the Z-axis was assumed as a baseline

steps.action: Checks the precision of the total-station reference from the repeated measurements: 0.2 mm in XY and 0.1 mm in Z.
steps.quote: The average positional variation for all targets and check points in the XY plane was 0.2 mm (σ = 0.13 mm).

steps.action: Compares check-point errors with the baseline for the uncalibrated measured-Z scenarios. A (all targets) and E (core-edge targets) are accurate; B, C and D (table targets) fail, and C and D are domed.
steps.quote: Reconstructions B, C and D all had an interquartile range (IQR) greater than the baseline.

steps.action: Attributes the domed reconstructions to failed SFM estimation of lens distortion in near-parallel photography, citing James and Robson (2014).
steps.quote: occurs when the SFM process fails to estimate accurately the lens distortion parameters (James and Robson 13)

steps.action: Runs reconstruction F with the secondary core-edge targets to confirm the XY result of E; F shows errors more in line with the other scenarios.
steps.quote: A second reconstruction (F), using the secondary edge targets, was performed to confirm the XY results of reconstruction E

steps.action: Repeats the target configurations with a pre-calibrated lens (G-L). Doming disappears and the table-target scenarios improve, except I (corner targets only), consistent with the lens-distortion explanation.
steps.quote: Reconstructions I and J showed none of the curved reconstruction seen in reconstructions C and D.

steps.action: Replaces measured target heights with assumed constant Z values (M-V). Most scenarios then fail the Z baseline; only S and U pass in both XY and Z.
steps.quote: Reconstructions M-V used assumed Z values for targets.

steps.action: Applies the targetless, calibrated-camera workflow to the real Lake Surprise cores. Reconstructed 100 mm tape lengths in 180 sections give a standard deviation of 0.33 mm.
steps.quote: The core photography of the Lake Surprise cores did not use targets.

steps.action: Concludes that lens calibration has the greatest influence on reconstruction quality: calibrated scenarios pass even with sparse control, while uncalibrated ones need plentiful or core-edge control.
steps.quote: The lens calibration appears to have the greatest influence on the quality of 3D reconstruction.

steps.action: Attributes the assumed-Z failures to the auxiliary (wrong target heights on the twisted beamcore distorting the fit), not to the photogrammetric method.
steps.quote: This variation in Z was expected, as the beamcore had an intentional twist

steps.action: Refines the result into a recommended user procedure: S, with table targets beside the core (for example on gridded paper), assumed Z, and a calibrated camera.
steps.quote: a general user who wishes to obtain high-quality orthometric core images without access to high-end measuring equipment should follow procedure S

steps.action: Proposes using the 3D mesh to flag damaged or non-representative core surfaces, illustrated with a PCV filter in CloudCompare on a damaged core.
steps.quote: they may be readily identifiable using spatially based techniques applied to the 3D mesh or point cloud (Fig. 7)

steps.action: Concludes that SFM-MVS is a versatile, efficient core-documentation method, that lens calibration is critical, and that well-defined targets beside the core improve reconstruction.
steps.quote: demonstrated that calibration of lens distortion characteristics was critical to maintaining accuracy of the 3D reconstruction

tree.answer: No new phenomenon; the known problem of topographic distortion in core photographs
Reconstruction errors measured directly against total-station check points
Characterize the accuracy of SFM-MVS core orthophotography across scenarios
No rival hypotheses; rival processing scenarios (targets, calibration, Z)
Only A and G expected as the upper accuracy limit; no other stated predictions
Conditions set in the lab (beamcore with a 4 mm twist, target layouts)
Partly: calibrated lens with table targets (H, S) survives; many configurations fail
Method kept and characterized; procedure S recommended

end.claim: SFM-MVS photogrammetry produces sediment-core orthophotos within 0.5 mm XY and 1 mm Z when the lens is pre-calibrated; table targets with assumed Z and a calibrated camera (procedure S) are a simple, accurate recipe.

decisive_move.sentence: Deliberately varying lens calibration, target configuration and assumed versus measured Z across 22 beamcore scenarios, scored against total-station check points, is what identifies calibration as critical and singles out procedure S.

gates.evidence: Action: no stated hypothesis directed data acquisition; the scenarios form a configuration grid (§2 ¶8-9). Claim: each scenario could fail the stated XY and Z baseline, and several did (B, C, D, I, M-R, T, V; §3 ¶3-6). Registration: the acceptance baseline and IQR rule are stated in Methods (§2 ¶8), but the paper does not say they were fixed before the errors were seen (inference).

imports.item: Structure from Motion–Multi-View Stereo reconstruction (Snavely et al. 2006)
Agisoft Metashape Pro, with COLMAP and MicMac named as alternatives
Consumer digital camera (Olympus E-M1 II) and raw processing in DXO Photolab
Leica TCRP 1203 total station with GMP101 mini prism
PCV (per-pixel visibility) filter (Tarini et al. 2003) in CloudCompare

novelty_claims.quote: We expand upon their work by quantifying the quality of 3D reconstruction and orthoimagery for 22 different SFM-MVS scenarios.
The results documented in this study present a solution that can provide accurate spatial control while also being simple to establish.

limits: No review file or earlier version was supplied, so there is no review sequence. The beamcore is a printed image on a wooden beam, not real sediment, and accuracy rests on six check points per scenario. The acceptance baseline is the authors' judgement ('what we consider would be reasonably achievable'); whether it was fixed before the errors were seen is not stated (inference). Only one camera, one lens and one focal length are tested. The real-core check (Lake Surprise) compares reconstructed lengths with the tape that also supplied the scale; no independent reference is used. There is no direct comparison with core scanners or centre-stripe methods, so the speed and cost advantages are argued, not measured. Sub-claims: the damage-detection use of the 3D mesh (Figure 7) is shown by one qualitative example (status none). The Lake Surprise length precision (0.33 mm SD) is an estimate_with_resolution. The claims about field or handheld use are untested. The novelty statements are extension claims, not explicit 'first' statements. Composition is none_fits: the walk is a problem-driven characterization of an existing capability, by a designed laboratory grid of auxiliary variations against a fixed baseline, with no rival hypotheses. capability_first is the closest fit, but the problem precedes the capability here.

disagreements.target: McMillan (2008) and centre-stripe or line-camera methods (Johnson 2015)
disagreements.support: Argument only: the stripe method needs many photos and limits overlap, so photography takes longer while the sediment oxidizes; no comparative test is run.
disagreements.quote: This technique necessitates the use of many tens to hundreds of photos per core segment, and restricts the potential overlap available for aligning and merging [...]

disagreements.target: Systems that move a core past a stationary camera (McMillan 2008)
disagreements.support: Argument that a moving background confuses SFM point matching, whereas a moving camera records the whole static scene; not tested.
disagreements.quote: In contrast to systems that move a core past a stationary camera (McMillan 16), this technique does not require any editing of photos

disagreements.target: Wide-angle focal length recommendation for photogrammetry (Marčiš 2013)
disagreements.support: Argues that core scenes are simple and that short telephoto lenses reduce occluded regions (Hobbie 1974); no test of focal length is made.
disagreements.quote: However, for sediment core photogrammetry, the scene is relatively simple, and usually presents little challenge for 3D reconstruction.

disagreements.target: Applying a lens-distortion correction before SFM-MVS (models such as Brown 1971)
disagreements.support: Argues that a double correction may cause problems; reports that both corrected and uncorrected images processed easily.
disagreements.quote: applying an additional lens distortion correction prior to SFM-MVS processing may cause problems

alternatives_considered.chosen: Short telephoto focal length (80 mm, 135-format equivalent)
alternatives_considered.reason: Simple scene; normal to short telephoto lenses reduce regions without data caused by obstruction

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Images corrected for lens distortion beforehand
alternatives_considered.reason: SFM-MVS models lens distortion itself; a double correction may cause problems
To avoid introducing artefacts into the imagery
none given (a similar workflow is said to be achievable)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Scraping the surface plus very diffuse bounced light against glare
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Cross polarisation, covering the core with thin plastic

alternatives_considered.chosen: About 15 photos per metre at about 7 cm spacing
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Fewer photos with greater coverage when speed matters more than resolution
alternatives_considered.reason: Target resolution of 0.05 mm per pixel

alternatives_considered.chosen: Check points on natural surface features (sand grains)
alternatives_considered.reason: To better replicate the influence of sediment colour and texture on the reconstruction

alternatives_considered.chosen: Procedure S (table targets, assumed Z, calibrated camera)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: The other 21 scenarios (target layouts, SFM-derived lens parameters, measured Z)
alternatives_considered.reason: Meets the XY and Z baseline without precision measurement tools and is simple to establish

alternatives_considered.chosen: Targetless photography of the Lake Surprise cores with a calibrated camera and a tape for scale
